parts.title: Learning to skateboard
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last summer, my cousin gave me his old skateboard. I had always wanted to try, but I never thought that I would be any good. On the first day, I fell off nine times in half an hour, and my knees were covered with bruises.

A girl called Noor was watching me from the bench. She came over and said, "You are leaning backwards. Bend your knees and look where you want to go." I tried again, and for the first time, I rolled across the path without falling.

After that, Noor and I met every day. She taught me how to push, turn and stop. She also told me to always wear a helmet, even for a short ride. "Everybody falls," she said. "The best skaters just fall less." That made me feel better.

Now, three months later, I can do a small jump called an ollie. It is not very high, but I am proud of it. Next month, there is a contest for beginners at the park, and Noor says that I should enter. I am not sure, but I might.

parts.title: The story of skateboarding
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Skateboarding began in California in the 1950s. [1] They were bored when the sea was flat, so they wanted something to do on land.

The first boards were simply wooden boxes on roller-skate wheels. [2] Later, people made them from solid planks, which were easier to control.

In the 1970s, a new kind of wheel made from plastic was invented. [3] Skateboarding became popular all over the world, and new parks were built.

In the 1980s, the sport became more dangerous. [4] Many parks were closed because they were too expensive to insure.

Today, skateboarding is back, and it will be part of the Olympic Games. [5] Experts say that more than eighty million people now ride boards worldwide.
sentences: It was a big improvement because the board gripped the ground better.
Some riders wear special shoes with flat soles.
They were rather heavy and not very comfortable.
This shows how much the sport has grown in seventy years.
Some young skaters tried high jumps and more risky tricks.
In some countries, it was banned by the government.
By 1965, more than fifty million boards had been sold.
The idea came from surfers looking for something to do.

gaps.explanation: The idea came from surfers; the next sentence says they were bored when the sea was flat.
The first boards were wooden boxes; they were heavy and uncomfortable.
The new wheel was a big improvement, and the next sentence says skating became popular.
Some skaters tried high jumps, which made the sport more dangerous.
This shows how much the sport has grown, after the number of riders.

parts.title: Safety first
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Skateboarding is great fun, but it can be dangerous if you are not careful. Every year, thousands of people hurt themselves [1] falling off their boards. The most common injuries are to the wrists, ankles and head. [2] this reason, experts say that you must always wear a helmet, knee pads and wrist guards. It is also important to check your board before every ride. The wheels should turn easily, [3] the screws should be tight. Choose a place where there are not [4] many people. A quiet park or an empty car park is better than a busy street. If you are a beginner, ask [5] experienced skater to show you the basic moves. Never try a trick that you cannot do, because it is easy to make a serious mistake. Finally, remember to stop when you feel tired. Many accidents happen at the end of a long session, when people are [6] longer paying attention.

gaps.explanation: Hurt themselves by falling: the means.
For this reason: a fixed phrase.
The wheels should turn easily, and the screws should be tight.
Not too many people: a fixed phrase.
An experienced skater: the indefinite article before a vowel.
No longer paying attention: a fixed phrase.

parts.title: A talk at a skate park
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: nathalie
turns.text: Hello, everyone, and welcome to the opening of our new skate park. My name is Noor, and I’m the manager. First, some facts. The park cost three hundred thousand pounds to build. The council paid one hundred thousand, and the rest came from local businesses and from people like you, who sold cakes. Let me describe the park. We planned four areas, but there was no space for the fourth, so there are three. The first is the bowl, for experienced skaters. The second is the street area, with steps and rails. And the third is a small, flat area for beginners and little children. Opening hours start at eight in the morning. The park closes at nine in the evening, because of the lights, and the neighbours asked us not to stay later. On Sundays we close earlier, at seven, but that’s the only day. You can hire a board for five pounds, but you don’t need to if you have your own. The helmet is compulsory, and it costs two pounds to hire. Without one, nobody can enter. Next, lessons. On Saturday morning we have a lesson for children aged ten to fourteen. Last year it was ten to twelve, but we received so many requests from teenagers that we changed it. On Sundays there are lessons for adults, over sixteen, but you must book. Finally, every month we hold a contest. The winner gets fifty pounds, and the person in second place gets twenty. Come and watch, because it’s a lot of fun. Thank you, and enjoy the park.

gaps.explanation: The council paid one hundred thousand, but the total cost was three hundred thousand pounds.

gaps.prompt: On most days the park shuts at ___ in the evening
gaps.explanation: On Sundays they close at seven, but every other day the park closes at nine.

gaps.prompt: The park is divided into ___ areas
gaps.explanation: They planned four areas, but there is space for three.
A board costs five pounds to hire; the helmet costs two pounds.

gaps.prompt: The Saturday lesson accepts children up to the age of ___
gaps.explanation: Last year the lesson was for ten to twelve, but it is now for ten to fourteen.

gaps.prompt: Each month the contest winner receives ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: The winner gets fifty pounds and the person in second place gets twenty.

parts.title: An interview with a professional skater
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Max, why did you begin to skate?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I would love to say that my school had a team, but we only had football. A friend of mine won a prize at some contest, a really nice board, and he showed it to me, but I wasn’t impressed. The truth is my sister. She’s four years older than me, and she skated everywhere. I followed her to the park every day because I wanted to be as good as her. She’s still better at some tricks, but don’t tell anyone.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: You need strength for the tricks. How do you keep strong?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: People assume that I swim, because swimmers are strong, and I do a few lengths on holiday, but not every morning. I go to the gym once a week to lift weights, and it helps, but it’s a small part. What really works is running in the hills every day. It builds my legs and my breathing, and it’s quiet up there. I take my dog, so he’s fitter than me.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: You broke your arm two years ago. What did you do during that time?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: It was the worst month of my life. I couldn’t take part in contests, and the sponsors said no problem, but I knew I was losing time. I didn’t travel either, because I had to stay near the hospital. So I studied. I watched hundreds of videos of other skaters, slowly, and I made notes about how they land. When the arm was better, I came back with ten new ideas.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you enjoy most about your life?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: The prizes are nice, and I have a shelf for them in my room, but I never look at it. The money is good, I won’t lie, and I have a nice flat thanks to it. But what I love is the freedom. On a board nobody tells you where to go or what to do. If I want to ride to the sea at midnight, I just do it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice do you give to young skaters?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Don’t buy the most expensive board. The shop assistant will tell you to, but a cheap one is fine to start. And skating in the evening is not a rule, you can skate whenever you can. My real advice is to be patient. A trick can take months to learn. Film yourself, and watch the video, because you will see mistakes that you can’t feel.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you want to do when you stop competing?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I would like to coach, maybe, because kids ask me all the time, but I’m not a patient teacher. A shop? My cousin has one, and the work is boring. What I dream about is building skate parks, designing the bowls and the rails, because I know what skaters like. I have drawn a few already, and the city asked me about one.
